'''Joram Piatigorsky''' (born February 24, 1940) is an American [[molecular biologist]] and eye researcher.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Joram Piatigorsky {{!}} Helen Keller Foundation|url = http://www.helenkellerfoundation.org/index.php?cID=161|website = www.helenkellerfoundation.org|accessdate = 2015-07-02}}</ref> He was the founding chief of the Laboratory of Molecular and Developmental Biology, [[National Eye Institute]], [[National Institutes of Health]] (1981–2009).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nei.nih.gov/intramural/joramp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207145634/https://www.nei.nih.gov/intramural/joramp|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 7, 2014|title = Research Labs and Branches &#124; National Eye Institute}}</ref> He is the recipient of the 2008 Helen Keller Prize for Vision Research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://helenkellerfoundation.org/joram-piatigorsky/|title=Joram Piatigorsky – Helen Keller Foundation}}</ref>

He is the son of cellist [[Gregor Piatigorsky]] and [[Jacqueline Piatigorsky|Jacqueline de Rothschild]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Piatgorsky House is Gone, But Pieces of History Were Saved |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 1, 2014 |url=http://www.latimes.com/local/great-reads/la-me-c1-piatigorsky-house-20141201-story.html }}</ref>

== Publications ==
Piatigorsky is the author of several books, including a scientific textbook, a memoir, a novel and a collection of short stories. Over the course of his career in science, he has published more than 300 scientific articles, reviews and book chapters on vision research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://helenkellerfoundation.org/joram-piatigorsky/|title=Joram Piatigorsky – Helen Keller Foundation}}</ref>

In ''Gene Sharing and Evolution: The Diversity of Protein Functions'' (Harvard University Press 2007),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hup.harvard.edu/catalog.php?isbn=9780674023413|title=Gene Sharing and Evolution — Joram Piatigorsky}}</ref> Piatigorsky summarized and extended his "[[Protein moonlighting|gene sharing]]" concept.<ref name="PIATIGORSKYPiatigorsky2009">{{cite book|author1=Joram PIATIGORSKY|author2=Joram Piatigorsky|title=Gene Sharing and Evolution: The Diversity of Protein Functions|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_4YaeCobdakC|date=30 June 2009|publisher=Harvard University Press|isbn=978-0-674-04212-4}}</ref>

He co-edited a book on an international symposium he organized: ''Molecular Biology of the Eye: Genes, Vision and Ocular Disease''.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Molecular biology of the eye, vol. 88: Genes, vision, and ocular disease|journal = American Journal of Human Genetics|date = 1989|issn = 0002-9297|pmc = 1683347|pages = 340|volume = 45|issue = 2|first1 = P.J.|last1 = Ringens|first2 = P.R.|last2 = Cotran}}</ref>

His debut novel, ''Jellyfish Have Eyes'' (IP Books, 2014), forewarns of the danger of reducing funding for basic research,<ref name="Piatigorsky2014">{{cite book|author=Joram Piatigorsky|title=Jellyfish Have Eyes|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eMaGoAEACAAJ|date=1 June 2014|publisher=International Psychoanalytic Books|isbn=978-0-9895622-6-3}}</ref> and has garnered positive reviews in the [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Science and Culture: Using fiction to make the case for basic research|journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date = 2015|issn = 0027-8424|pmid = 25852137|pages = 4185–4186|volume = 112|issue = 14|doi = 10.1073/pnas.1502378112|first = Joel|last = Shurkin|pmc=4394243|bibcode = 2015PNAS..112.4185S|doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = NEI Scientist Emeritus's Debut Novel Probes Jellyfish Eyes - The NIH Record - May 8, 2015|url = http://nihrecord.nih.gov/newsletters/2015/05_08_2015/story4.htm|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150714084134/http://nihrecord.nih.gov/newsletters/2015/05_08_2015/story4.htm|url-status = dead|archive-date = July 14, 2015|website = nihrecord.nih.gov|accessdate = 2015-06-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Narrative NIH scientist enters literary world -- Gazette.Net|url = http://www.gazette.net/article/20141029/ENTERTAINMENT/141029216/1124/narrative-nih-scientist-enters-literary-world&template=gazette|accessdate = 2015-06-25|url-status = dead|archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20150714100328/http://www.gazette.net/article/20141029/ENTERTAINMENT/141029216/1124/narrative-nih-scientist-enters-literary-world%26template%3Dgazette|archivedate = 2015-07-14}}</ref>

In his memoir, ''The Speed of Dark'' (Adelaide Books, 2018), Piatigorsky reflects on his 50-year career as a scientific researcher and describes how his family's pursuit of excellence and his father's quest for musical perfection influenced and inspired his own scientific career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/joram-piatigorsky/the-speed-of-darka/|title = THE SPEED OF DARK &#124; Kirkus Reviews}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://politics-prose.d7.indiebound.com/event/book/joram-piatigorsky-speed-of-dark-memoir|title = Joram Piatigorsky - the Speed of Dark: A Memoir &#124; Politics and Prose Bookstore}}</ref>
